[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Filestore: Network File System (NFS) on Google Cloud"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Filestore is a fully managed Network File System (NFS) service on Google Cloud Platform (GCP). It provides persistent, shared storage for applications that require NFS. This tutorial will guide you through the basics of using Filestore."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The Cloud SDK installed and configured."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of NFS and Linux file systems."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enable the Filestore API"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before you can use Filestore, you need to enable the Filestore API in your GCP project. You can do this through the Google Cloud Console or using the gcloud command-line tool."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"gcloud services enable file.googleapis.com"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Create a Filestore Instance"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, create a Filestore instance. You'll need to specify the instance name, tier, file share name, capacity, and network."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"gcloud filestore instances create <instance-name> \
    --zone=<zone> \
    --tier=<tier> \
    --file-share=name=<file-share-name>,capacity=<capacity-gib> \
    --network=name=default"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace the following placeholders:"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"<instance-name>: The name of your Filestore instance."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"<zone>: The zone where you want to create the instance (e.g., us-central1-a)."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"<tier>: The service tier (e.g., basic-ssd, enterprise)."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"<file-share-name>: The name of the file share (e.g., vol1)."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"<capacity-gib>: The capacity of the file share in GiB (e.g., 1024)."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Mount the Filestore Instance on a Compute Engine VM"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"To use the Filestore instance, you need to mount it on a Compute Engine VM. First, get the IP address of the Filestore instance."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"gcloud filestore instances describe <instance-name> --zone=<zone> --format="value(networks.ipAddresses[0])""},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace <instance-name> and <zone> with the appropriate values. Then, SSH into your Compute Engine VM and install the NFS client."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nfs-common"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a mount point and mount the Filestore instance."},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"sudo mkdir /mnt/filestore
sudo mount <filestore-ip>:/<file-share-name> /mnt/filestore"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace <filestore-ip> with the IP address you obtained earlier and <file-share-name> with the file share name you specified when creating the instance."},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"To make the mount persistent across reboots, add an entry to /etc/fstab."},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"echo '<filestore-ip>:/<file-share-name> /mnt/filestore nfs defaults 0 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab"},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Verify the Mount"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Verify that the Filestore instance is mounted correctly."},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"df -h /mnt/filestore"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command should show the mounted Filestore instance and its available space."},{"order":33,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Clean Up"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"To avoid incurring unnecessary charges, delete the Filestore instance when you're finished."},{"order":35,"type":"code","text":"gcloud filestore instances delete <instance-name> --zone=<zone>"},{"order":36,"type":"paragraph","text":"Also, remove the entry from /etc/fstab and unmount the file system."},{"order":37,"type":"code","text":"sudo umount /mnt/filestore
sudo sed -i '/<filestore-ip>:/<file-share-name>/d' /etc/fstab"},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a basic introduction to using Filestore on Google Cloud. For more advanced configurations and features, refer to the official Google Cloud documentation."}]
